narrative:
The machine learning model predicted an 83% chance that you would fail the bar exam, which is a significant concern for your application to law school. This high probability of failure is a strong indicator that the admissions committee felt it was unlikely you would succeed in the rigorous environment of law school and subsequently on the bar exam.

The decision to deny your application was primarily influenced by three key factors. First, your academic performance in your third year placed you in a lower decile compared to accepted students, indicating that your grades were below average for those who successfully passed the bar exam. This suggests that your academic trajectory may not have been strong enough to prepare you for the challenges ahead.

Second, your choice to work part-time while studying may have contributed to the prediction of failure. Most successful applicants tend to work full-time, which often allows them to focus more on their studies. Balancing work and school can be demanding, and this could have impacted your academic performance.

Lastly, your family income bracket, while not a direct measure of capability, can reflect the resources available to support your education. The majority of accepted students come from upper-middle-income families, which may provide additional academic support and opportunities.

To improve your chances in the future, consider focusing on enhancing your academic performance, possibly by dedicating more time to your studies or seeking additional support. Additionally, evaluating your work commitments could help you better balance your responsibilities.
